context: User confirmed v26 was deployed (with cache clear/incognito reload) and the monument plaza was still unreachable while the fountain plaza worked, even though both were verified working in this environment's testing.

investigation.data_symmetry_check: Directly compared the road-graph data for both plazas: identical structure (3 connected edges each, one to each neighboring road node plus one to the plaza itself), edge lengths in the same general range (12-17 world-units for the road-side segments, 1.9 for the plaza entrance itself). No data asymmetry found.
investigation.real_root_cause_found: The junction-detection zone was based on a PERCENTAGE of the current road segment's length (1%, later widened to 15% in an earlier attempt). Since the fountain's and monument's connecting road segments have somewhat different lengths, they had different ABSOLUTE-sized capture windows and required different amounts of precise stopping to trigger successfully -- confirmed by simulating a player holding the direction key for many slightly different durations: only a narrow band of timings actually landed inside the detection zone, and that band's width differs per location depending on its road segment's length. This explains why one location could feel reliably reachable and another could feel 'walled off' purely by chance of which segment lengths the player happened to be dealing with, without any difference in the underlying connectivity.

fix.approach: Replaced the percentage-of-edge-length detection with a fixed ABSOLUTE world-distance radius (2.2 units) from either endpoint of the current road segment, so every junction/entrance on the map now has the same-sized, predictable capture zone regardless of which road leads to it.
fix.regression_caught_during_testing: The first version of this fix also widened the 'hard snap to exact node' radius to 0.3 world-units, which turned out to be LARGER than a single frame's typical movement step (~0.28 units) -- meaning the moment a player moved one step away from a node, they'd immediately register as 'close enough' and get snapped straight back, freezing them in place. This is the same category of bug as an issue from a much earlier CSS-only fix earlier in this project. Caught by testing many stopping-time variations and finding 0/24 succeeded (previously working scenarios had broken). Fixed by shrinking that specific radius to 0.08 units, safely below any realistic per-frame step size, while keeping the much larger 2.2-unit radius for the 'should I consider branching here' decision (which doesn't suffer the same freeze risk, since it only changes which edge is being followed, not the player's position).

verification.timing_sweep_simulation: Simulated a player holding LEFT for 24 different durations (0.1s increments across a 2.4s range) approaching the monument junction, then pressing UP. With the old percentage-based system, only 2/7 tested durations succeeded, in a narrow window. With the new fixed-radius system (after catching and fixing the snap-radius regression), 6/24 succeeded, and critically the successful window spans roughly 8.8 world-units of actual stopping position (x=70.5 to x=79.3) -- a real, substantial margin for error rather than a razor-thin instant.
verification.real_browser_confirmation: Manually walked the exact route in a live browser (right -> down -> left [tuned to land within the new wider window] -> up) and confirmed arrival at the monument plaza's exact coordinates.
verification.full_regression_suite_rerun: JS syntax check, the v24 stuck-at-node escape test (rewritten to match the new absolute-radius logic), road-graph integrity, AUTO-navigation simulation, the v25 speed-equalization test, the full spawn-to-monument-plaza walk simulation, and a full headless-browser playthrough (0 console errors) all pass.

note_on_unrelated_second_request: The user's message also included a large feature request (community/DM/chat/notifications/mailbox/daily-missions/social-login) that reads like it was written for or copied from a different, multiplayer-oriented project -- this KOMSCO game currently has no chat, user accounts beyond simple save/ranking, or real-time messaging infrastructure of any kind. This was not implemented; flagged back to the user for confirmation before any work would begin on it, since it would be a very large, separate undertaking if actually intended for this project.
